primitives.name: Probability Estimation Form
primitives.verbatim_quote: The individual, as already observed, throws his estimate of the value of an opinion into the probability form of "a successes in b trials" (a/b being a proper fraction) and "feels" toward it as toward any other probability situation.

primitives.assumptions: Subjective estimation follows empirical frequency model.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When b → ∞, \hat{p} converges to true probability p.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that while grouping instances eliminates uncertainty through statistical convergence, individual decisions remain indistinguishable in behavior regardless of whether risk or uncertainty is present. This duality implies that for singular events, the mathematical treatment of risk and uncertainty collapses into equivalent decision frameworks. The estimation form \hat{p} = a/b provides a foundational bridge between subjective belief and objective frequency, enabling both Bayesian inference and dynamic decision modeling. The failure mode occurs when the number of trials is insufficient to approximate true probability, leading to overconfidence in estimates. The epistemic structure supports recursive reasoning where each decision contributes to a larger ensemble, yet retains individual agency. This creates a dual logic: ensemble-based risk mitigation and individualized uncertainty handling.
